summary: Prefetch timeout during canary prewarm unbinds tenant pin and routes to degraded fallback
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart observed that during a staged canary for rlhf-v2-13b, a tenant that had an explicit model version pin was routed to a degraded fallback variant after a prewarm/prefetch step timed out. Impact: production requests for three BrightCart API keys returned responses from a degraded lightweight variant, causing a drop in quality and downstream business impact (search relevance regression).

Impact:
- ~450 affected requests over a 7 minute window (customer monitoring)
- Quality regression alerts triggered (BrightCart QA)
- One customer complaint to CS escalated to P1

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dc-dedicated-us-east-2 (prod)
- Canary slice: weight 5% for rlhf-v2-13b -> rolling prewarm to new kernel
- Client: BrightCart, dedicated capacity, tenant-level pin set to redwood/rlhf-v2-13b@2026-03-09-15:22

Observed behavior:
- Prewarm/prefetch stage attempted to warm KV cache on canary host but prewarm agent returned timeout (prefetch timeout code 504-prefetch)
- Orchestrator subsequently considered the prewarm incomplete and triggered fallback routing for incoming tenant requests
- Tenant pin metadata expected to prevent fallback was not honored for ~6m, requests routed to lightweight fallback variant instead

Why this is high priority:
- Dedicated customers expect pin to be respected during canary operations
- Quality regressions and potential revenue impact for customer-facing features
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer has tenant-level pin to specific model version.
2) Trigger a canary rollout that prewarms a small percentage (5%) of traffic to a new host/kernel.
3) Force a delayed prewarm response (simulated network delay) or inject a prewarm timeout in the prewarm agent.
4) Observe routing for pinned tenant during and after prewarm timeout window (expectation: keep pinned variant; observed: fallback to degraded variant).

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: prewarm timeout triggered orchestrator health gating which temporarily removed the canary host from the eligible set. The routing layer applied host-level health decisions before consulting tenant pin metadata, so steering logic allowed fallback to a compatible but degraded variant.

Findings so far:
- Pin metadata resides in control-plane snapshot; snapshot read by orchestrator during reconcile. Snapshot remained unchanged.
- Timing window: routing decision path consults host health -> eligible variants selection -> then tenant pin reconciliation. Race: if host removed from eligibility before pin bound was enforced for the request, routing falls back.
- Different code paths: streaming long-lived sessions vs per-request selection show variance: streaming sessions preserved pin affinity, short HTTP requests were more likely to hit fallback.
- Prefetch agent returned 504-prefetch on three prewarm attempts; network flakiness suspected between prewarm agent and kernel host.

Open action items:
- Add guard in routing: check tenant pin earlier in the decision graph and consider 'prefer-pinned-variant' flag during canary prewarm windows.
- Increase prewarm timeout and add conservative retry logic for prewarm agent on dedicated pools.
- Add telemetry to count 'pin-blocked-by-host-health' events.
- Run integration test that simulates prewarm timeout and asserts pin is honored.

Diego Martinez (SRE): 2026-03-10 16:25 - Reproduced in staging with delayed prewarm response. Confirmed routing path favors host-health before pin metadata. Preparing a mitigation patch to consult pin earlier.

Elena Huang (Platform Eng): 2026-03-11 09:45 - Investigating prewarm-agent logs; observed network hiccups to kernel host. Proposed backoff+retry and temp increase of prewarm timeout for dedicated clusters.

BrightCart (Customer): 2026-03-11 12:02 - Thanks for the update. Can you confirm whether we will see a rollback if an in-flight prewarm fails? We need guarantees that our pinned traffic won't see degraded variants.
Diego Martinez (SRE): 2026-03-11 12:30 - Short-term workaround: set tenant pin enforcement to 'strict' for BrightCart via console (we'll toggle from support). Long-term fix tracked in ORCH-4721.
resolution_summary:
Mitigation applied: temporarily set BrightCart tenant pin enforcement to strict to prefer pinned variant even when host health is degraded; increased prewarm-agent timeout to 12s for the affected dedicated pool and added 2 retry attempts. Patch queued: orchestrator PR to re-order routing decision to consult tenant pin earlier (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/391).

Follow-ups:
- ORCH-4721: reorder routing decision graph to prefer pinned variants during canary prewarm windows (owner: Elena Huang, ETA 2026-03-18).
- Add regression test in CI to simulate prewarm timeout and assert pinned routing (owner: Diego Martinez, ETA 2026-03-20).
- Postmortem scheduled if issue recurs after patch (owner: Support Lead).
final_resolution_status: Workaround live; code change pending merge and rollout
